What land is used for (farming, forestry, tourism)
Paths worn away by too many walkers
Tourism that protects landscape and locals

walkthroughs.body_html:
UK's largest national park, NW England. Classic glacial scenery: ribbon lakes (Windermere, Ullswater), U-shaped valleys, corries, England's highest peak Scafell Pike (978m).

UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2017. Around 18 million visitors per year.

Tourism: hotels, cafes, boat hire, climbing — biggest employer.

Hill sheep farming: Herdwick sheep — vital for landscape and culture.

Forestry: conifer plantations e.g. Whinlatter, Grizedale.

Quarrying: slate quarries at Honister.

Traffic: narrow lanes jammed in summer.
Footpath erosion: hills like Helvellyn worn bare.
House prices: second homes price out locals.
Farming vs tourism: walkers and dogs disturb livestock.

Solutions: Fix the Fells path repairs, park-and-ride, affordable housing schemes, off-season marketing.
